questions.q: What is the most accurate way to describe an OWASP Top 10 entry like "Injection"?
options: A risk category covering many related, specific testable weaknesses that share a root cause
A single automated test that either passes or fails
A list of exact CVE numbers to check against
A legal requirement enforced by the CFAA
questions.explain: Each Top 10 entry is a risk category, not one test. "Injection" covers SQL, OS command, LDAP, and XSS wherever untrusted input reaches an interpreter unsanitized — a tester walks every relevant input, not a single checkbox.

questions.q: In the current OWASP Top 10:2025, what happened to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF), which was its own category in older material?
options: It was removed from the Top 10 entirely with no replacement
It was merged into A01:2025 Broken Access Control
It became its own new A10 category
It was renamed Cryptographic Failures
questions.explain: SSRF now lives inside A01:2025 Broken Access Control, since SSRF is fundamentally a server making a request it shouldn't have been authorized to make.

questions.q: Which category is new in the OWASP Top 10:2025 edition and covers risks across an application's entire build and distribution pipeline, not just outdated libraries?
options: A09:2025 Logging & Alerting Failures
A06:2025 Insecure Design
A03:2025 Software Supply Chain Failures
A04:2025 Cryptographic Failures
questions.explain: A03:2025 Software Supply Chain Failures broadens the older "vulnerable and outdated components" idea into the whole chain: dependencies, unsigned build artifacts, and compromised CI/CD steps.

questions.q: Why would a tester scope deeper A07:2025 Authentication Failures testing on a banking API but spend very little time on it for a static marketing site?
options: Authentication testing is always required equally regardless of the application
Static sites are legally exempt from authentication testing
The OWASP Top 10 only applies to applications with a login page
Scope, time budget, and the application's own architecture determine where testing depth actually matters
questions.explain: Not every category gets equal depth on every engagement. A static content site has little authentication surface to test, while a banking API's risk is concentrated in access control, cryptography, and authentication.

questions.q: Why is citing "A05" alone, with no further detail, not considered a real finding in a penetration test report?
options: Because A05 refers to Insecure Design, which cannot be tested
Because category numbers are confidential and cannot appear in client reports
Because a real finding must name the specific vulnerability and location — the category number is only used to map that finding back for the risk conversation
Because OWASP category numbers change every week
questions.explain: A real report cites the specific vulnerability, such as a SQL injection in a specific parameter, and then maps it to the relevant OWASP category for context — not the category number by itself.
